memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Your threshing will continue until grape harvest and the grape harvest
will continue until planting, and you will eat all the food you want and
live in safety in your land'" - Lev 26:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God pictures a harvest so abundant that one season's work runs right into
the next. There would be no anxious gaps, no fearful stretches of empty
storehouses. Enough food, and safety in the land.

Again we hold this in its covenant setting. This was God's promise to
national Israel, not a guarantee that every faithful believer will always
have plenty and never face danger. We must not build a prosperity theology
on these verses.

But look beneath the material picture to the longing it expresses:
satisfaction and security. Every human heart wants these two things — to
be truly satisfied and to feel truly safe. Israel was to find both in a
right relationship with God.

Dear friend, here is where the New Covenant speaks powerfully. The deepest
satisfaction and security we crave are found not in circumstances but in
Christ. Jesus said, whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever
believes in me will never be thirsty (John 6:35). He spoke of a peace the
world cannot give (John 14:27).

Paul, often hungry and imprisoned, could still write that he had learned
to be content in any and every situation (Phil 4:11-12). His satisfaction
did not depend on his circumstances but on his Saviour.

You may not have outward abundance. But in Christ, the deepest hungers of
your soul can be filled and the deepest fears settled.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I looking for satisfaction and security?
2. Have I found genuine contentment in Christ, apart from circumstances?
3. What fear could I bring to the God who offers true safety?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, my heart longs to be satisfied and safe. Teach me to find both in
You rather than in my circumstances, resting in the peace that only Christ
gives. Amen.
